assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bringing macroscopic mechanical oscillators into their quantum ground state, and entangling and squeezing them, speaks directly to where the boundary between the quantum and the everyday world lies. It is a conceptually clean and fundamental advance, not a technology-driven one, and it is plainly new physics in the sense that the ground state and non-classical states of a visible object were not obviously reachable.
assessment.attribution: Several decisive experiments are credited: ground-state preparation in a piezoelectric resonator (Cleland), sideband cooling and squeezing in microwave circuit optomechanics (Teufel), and cavity optomechanics at the quantum level (Kippenberg, with Aspelmeyer and Painter close behind). Five credited names do not fit into three, so any trio leaves out a major contributor. My choice of three is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Results have been reproduced by several independent groups on different platforms (superconducting, photonic crystal, levitated and membrane systems) and the interpretation is stable. A prize is timely since the field has matured beyond first demonstrations.
uncertainties: Which three of the five credited people have priority is unresolved, and the first ground-state demonstrations were near-simultaneous.
I am not certain of the exact order and dates of the key experiments and have not verified them.
Application impact (sensing, transduction) is still developing, but the prize case rests on fundamental physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines the magic-wavelength idea with many atoms interrogated at once, giving fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. This is precision measurement of the kind I value most: close agreement between theory and experiment, tests of fundamental constants and relativity (gravitational redshift at the millimetre scale), and a path to a redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated it, and Ye's group carried the strontium clock to record accuracy and coherence. Two credited names give a clean configuration. Other groups (JILA and others, ion clocks by Wineland-type work already recognised) exist but the supplied credit supports a fair two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories worldwide operate lattice clocks and agree with each other, and international comparisons are routine. The field is very mature and the recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Wineland's 2012 prize already recognised ion-based optical clocks, so the committee must judge how much is new.
Whether Ye should be recognised here or for ultracold molecules, since he appears on both candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the foundations of quantum mechanics, namely no-cloning, entanglement and Bell nonlocality, into a protocol whose security rests on physical law. The idea is original and clear, and it has a lasting influence. Though I am drawn to the foundational side and not the technology, the 2022 prize on entanglement experiments makes this a natural continuation.
assessment.attribution: BB84 (Bennett and Brassard) and the entanglement-based protocol (Ekert) are the conceptual core. Pan's satellite and network experiments are a separate, later experimental achievement, and four credited names exceed three. Leaving out Pan is defensible but contentious.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are decades old and have been implemented by many groups, including field and satellite links. Security proofs and practical device loopholes (side channels) remain active, so claims of real-world security are not fully settled.
uncertainties: The proper balance between the theoretical founders and the experimental global-network work by Pan.
Practical security of implementations versus the idealised protocols is not something I can assess in detail.
Whether the committee regards this as physics or as computer science and cryptography.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation (Blatt and others) established a precise, controllable quantum many-body platform whose fidelities exceed those of nearly any other. It is built on exactly the atomic-physics toolbox I know, and its success rests on careful theory-experiment agreement.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the original theoretical proposal and Blatt led key experimental realisations. Wineland's group (already a laureate) and others such as Monroe made major contributions, so the credit is entangled with the 2012 prize and with the near-duplicate entry on atomic quantum information processing.
assessment.maturity: Independent ion-trap groups and companies have reproduced and scaled the work, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, but the 2012 prize overlaps part of the subject.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize (Wineland, Haroche) and with another ballot entry listing the same three names.
Whether Monroe, Wineland-type contributions or others should be credited is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Creating and characterising strongly interacting Fermi gases, with the BEC-BCS crossover, Feshbach resonances and the universal thermodynamics at unitarity, gave an ultra-clean testing ground for many-body physics connecting to superfluids, neutron matter and high-temperature superconductivity. It is fundamental, quantitatively tested and pedagogically beautiful.
assessment.attribution: Grimm, Salomon and Ketterle's groups all produced decisive early results on molecular condensates and pairing, and Jin and Thomas also made key contributions that are outside the supplied names. A two-name choice leaves out Ketterle, who is already a laureate, which is practical but leaves the credit incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Results have been reproduced by many groups and the thermodynamics is quantitatively confirmed. Recognition is timely and the field is mature.
uncertainties: Deborah Jin's death and the absence of Thomas from the credited names complicate a fair attribution.
How much new Nobel-level insight remains beyond the 2001 condensate prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cooling and controlling molecules, including direct laser cooling, buffer-gas beams and quantum-state-resolved collisions and chemistry, opens precision tests of fundamental symmetries (the electron electric dipole moment limits from ACME) and new quantum simulation platforms with long-range interactions. It is original and important, but the overall discovery is a set of techniques more than one single clear discovery.
assessment.attribution: DeMille, Doyle and Ye are all central, though Ye is also credited with the lattice clock. The creation of ground-state polar molecules from ultracold atoms is credited elsewhere in the field (Jin and Ye, and others) and is not fully captured by these three.
assessment.maturity: Independent groups now laser-cool and trap diatomic and polyatomic molecules, and electron EDM bounds have been repeated. Still, the most spectacular goals (quantum simulation with dipolar molecules) are still developing, so some of the recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: The compound character of the topic and where the decisive discovery lies.
Whether the electron EDM results, which are bounds and not discoveries, support a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: X-ray free-electron lasers deliver femtosecond, intense, coherent X-ray pulses, which let one study inner-shell processes and nonlinear X-ray physics in atoms and watch structural dynamics directly. They are important to my own area through time-resolved inner-shell vacancy studies. The underlying SASE concept is original and has had lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: The attribution is hard: the SASE idea (Kondratenko-Saldin, Bonifacio-Pellegrini-Narducci), the accelerator design (Kim, Rossbach and others) and the machines (LCLS, FLASH, European XFEL) involve many people, so a three-person prize is uncertain. Names supplied may leave out key early theorists.
assessment.maturity: Several facilities operate worldwide and results are well reproduced. Recognition is timely, though a significant fraction of the value is instrumental, which makes me hesitate compared with a clear discovery.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among the early theorists, the accelerator builders and the facility leaders.
Whether an instrument or technique, as opposed to a discovery, is the right object for the physics prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observing Anderson localization of matter waves in a controlled disorder gives a clean, direct view of a fundamental wave phenomenon that was long obscured in solids by interactions and decoherence. It is original and conceptually clear, and connects to the quantum-versus-classical question through wave interference.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 observations came from two groups, Aspect's group with a speckle potential and Inguscio's group with a quasi-periodic lattice. Aspect is already a laureate (2022), which may weigh against a second prize, and the one-dimensional versus three-dimensional (Delande, Müller, Bouyer and others) results are not all credited here.
assessment.maturity: The observations were confirmed in several groups and extended to three dimensions, and the interpretation is well understood. It is mature, though the scientific impact is somewhat narrower than the other candidates above.
uncertainties: The theoretical contribution of those who predicted the conditions is not included in the supplied credit.
The overall significance is moderate relative to the other entries and I am uncertain how the committee would weigh it.
